topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and outlines how previously introduced immune components integrate to initiate and resolve inflammation.

topics.label: Principles of innate immune recognition and danger sensing
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system detects infection and cellular damage by distinguishing self from non-self using PAMPs, DAMPs, and germline-encoded receptors.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptor families and activation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the specific classes of pattern recognition receptors, their intracellular signaling mechanisms, and the activation of the inflammasome complex.

topics.label: Inflammatory cell recruitment, trafficking, and systemic pathology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the cellular and vascular events of acute inflammation, including leukocyte extravasation, lymphatic drainage, and the pathological hazards of systemic cytokine release.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how inflammatory responses are turned off, how tissues heal and scar, and how persistent irritation leads to chronic inflammation and granulomas.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the presentation and announces the subject of the upcoming lecture.
